incidents.title: Waymo robotaxi drives into flooded road and is swept into creek; 3,791-vehicle voluntary NHTSA recall
incidents.system: Waymo autonomous driving system, 5th and 6th generation (Jaguar I-PACE platform)
incidents.description: On April 20, 2026, an unoccupied Waymo robotaxi operating in San Antonio, Texas, encountered an untraversable flooded section of road during heavy rainfall. Rather than stopping or rerouting, the system slowed but continued into the floodwater; the vehicle was subsequently swept into Salado Creek and had to be recovered days later. A second flood-related incident near McCullough Avenue and Contour Drive had occurred approximately two weeks earlier. Waymo paused San Antonio operations following the April 20 incident. On April 30, 2026, Waymo filed a voluntary software recall with NHTSA covering 3,791 vehicles equipped with 5th and 6th generation ADS across all operating cities (Phoenix, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Austin, San Antonio, and Atlanta). NHTSA announced the recall publicly on May 12, 2026. Waymo identified an area of improvement regarding untraversable flooded lanes specific to higher-speed roadways and is deploying an OTA software fix with refined extreme weather operations and restricted access to flash flood-prone areas. No passengers were on board at the time of either flood incident; no injuries were reported. This is Waymo's fifth recall since February 2024.

incidents.title: Avride delivery robot strikes and injures cyclist in Jersey City NJ, continues delivery route without stopping
incidents.system: Avride autonomous delivery robot (model unspecified; ~150 lb, Uber Eats deployment)
incidents.description: An Avride delivery robot (Uber Eats deployment) pulled into a Jersey City street directly into the path of cyclist Conor Shannon. Shannon was struck, knocked unconscious in mid-air, and sustained a broken shoulder and head injury. The robot did not stop at the scene; it continued its delivery route. Witness Sarah Ahern physically blocked the robot with her leg to document it before it continued. Shannon subsequently filed a lawsuit against Uber and Avride. Avride declined to comment, citing active litigation, but stated their fleet operates in accordance with traffic laws and safety regulations. The incident highlights a failure-to-yield error in the robot's intersection navigation logic and a post-collision behavioral gap: the system had no mechanism to detect collision with a human and halt. The incident adds to a growing Avride safety record: the company is simultaneously under NHTSA investigation for 16 robotaxi crashes in Texas (AV-010/EAISI-057) and had a prior pedestrian contact incident in Philadelphia (DEL-004/EAISI-056). Incident date reported approximately May 2026 (News12 NJ article published May 11, 2026); exact incident date not confirmed in available sources.

incidents.title: Avride robotaxi fleet: 16 crashes in Dallas and Austin TX (Dec 2025–Mar 2026); NHTSA formal investigation opened May 8 2026
incidents.system: Avride autonomous robotaxi (Hyundai Ioniq 5 with Avride autonomous driving system); Uber ride-hailing partnership
incidents.description: Between December 3, 2025 (Avride public launch in Dallas) and March 2026, Avride robotaxis were involved in 16 crashes across Dallas and Austin, Texas. One minor injury was recorded in December 2025 when a vehicle clipped an open pickup truck door; the victim did not require hospitalisation. Identified crash behaviours included: improper lane changes into adjacent vehicles, failure to slow or stop for slow-moving or stationary vehicles ahead, inadequate response to vehicles entering the lane, and striking stationary objects partially obstructing the lane. NHTSA characterised the vehicles as displaying excessive assertiveness and insufficient capability. All 16 crashes occurred with a safety monitor present in the driver seat; only one monitor intervention attempt was recorded. On May 8, 2026, NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation opened a formal investigation into Avride following preliminary video review of all 16 crashes. Avride stated it had implemented targeted technical and operational mitigations and that incident frequency relative to mileage had declined. Avride operates via an Uber app integration and had launched its Dallas robotaxi service December 3, 2025. Note: Avride also operates autonomous delivery robots in Philadelphia (see EAISI-056, DEL-004); this entry concerns the separate robotaxi platform.

incidents.title: Ukrainian AI-Controlled Autonomous FPV Quadcopter Drones Kill Russian Soldiers Without Human Oversight: First Confirmed Fully Autonomous Combat Action
incidents.system: Ukrainian AI-controlled autonomous FPV quadcopter drones (manufacturer unidentified by reporting; drone maker Alexander Kokhanovskyy disclosed test at Ukrainian embassy press event June 2026)
incidents.operator: Unidentified Ukrainian drone manufacturer (Alexander Kokhanovskyy identified as maker at disclosure event)
incidents.location: Near Bakhmut and Chasiv Yar, Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine (eastern front line)
incidents.description: In approximately 2024, Ukrainian forces conducted a test involving ten AI-controlled FPV quadcopter drones operating with no human in the decision loop at any stage: the drones were launched toward the eastern front line near Bakhmut and Chasiv Yar, covered approximately 3–5 kilometres over roughly 10 minutes, then entered what the drone maker described as 'Terminator mode' — a state in which an onboard AI model independently sought out, identified, and attacked human targets with no human input. Human-piloted survey drones dispatched afterward observed the aftermath, which the drone maker characterised as 'everything dead': approximately 'a couple' of dead Russian soldiers and one destroyed truck were identified. The incident was disclosed publicly for the first time at a press event hosted by the Ukrainian embassy in June 2026, where Alexander Kokhanovskyy — identified as the manufacturer — confirmed the test to New Scientist. Kokhanovskyy described the test as singular and unscaled; he acknowledged Ukraine officially maintains a ban on fully autonomous final-stage lethal targeting by drones, and stated this capability was not deployed at wider scale. The June 2026 disclosure marks the first publicly confirmed instance of fully autonomous AI systems independently selecting and killing human combatants in armed conflict without any human authorising individual targeting decisions.

incidents.title: Hugging Face LeRobot critical RCE vulnerability (CVE-2026-25874): unauthenticated pickle deserialization exposes physical robot actuator control paths
incidents.system: Hugging Face LeRobot open-source embodied AI and VLA framework, version 0.4.3 through 0.5.1
incidents.description: On April 28, 2026, researchers publicly disclosed CVE-2026-25874 (CVSS 9.3 Critical), an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Hugging Face LeRobot (version ≤0.5.1). The flaw resides in the async inference PolicyServer component: pickle.loads() is used to deserialize data arriving over unauthenticated gRPC channels with no TLS. An attacker with network access can send a crafted pickle payload through SendPolicyInstructions, SendObservations, or GetActions gRPC calls to execute arbitrary code on the host. The PolicyServer sits directly in the physical robot control path—its outputs govern actuator commands on robotic joints—meaning successful exploitation could allow an attacker to issue arbitrary motor-control instructions to connected robots, posing potential physical harm to nearby personnel and equipment. The vulnerability was independently discovered by researcher 'chenpinji' in December 2025 and separately reported to Hugging Face; it was publicly disclosed April 28, 2026. The flaw remained unpatched at disclosure, with a fix planned for version 0.6.0. LeRobot's own team had previously created Safetensors specifically because pickle is unsafe for ML model serialization, yet the network-facing PolicyServer deserialized attacker-controlled input via pickle.loads() with a nosec comment suppressing the static analysis warning. LeRobot is used in academic and commercial robotics research contexts including manipulation arms, mobile platforms, and humanoid robot development.

incidents.title: Russian Geran-2 Loitering Munition Strikes Galati Apartment Building: First Documented Civilian Casualties on NATO Soil from a Russian Autonomous Strike Drone
incidents.system: Russian Geran-2 (GPS-guided loitering munition; Russian production of Iranian-designed Shahed-136)
incidents.description: Early on May 29, 2026, a Russian Geran-2 GPS-guided loitering munition — launched as part of an overnight Russian strike targeting civilian and infrastructure targets in Ukraine's Odesa region — deviated from its intended flight path and struck a 10-storey residential apartment building in Galati, eastern Romania. The drone's full explosive warhead detonated on impact, igniting a fire on the roof. Two residents were injured: a woman sustained first-degree burns and a 14-year-old experienced an acute stress reaction; both were treated at Galati County Emergency Clinical Hospital. Romania's Ministry of National Defense confirmed the drone's identity as a Russian Geran-2, verified via serial numbers of on-site components. Romanian officials attributed the navigational deviation to technical failure or electronic warfare interference, specifically GPS jamming or spoofing, which disrupted the drone's autonomous navigation system during its mission over Ukraine. The incident constitutes the 28th documented breach of Romanian airspace by Russian drones during the Ukraine conflict and the first to produce documented civilian casualties inside a NATO member state. Romania declared the Russian consul in Constanta persona non grata, closed Russia's Constanta consulate, and convened an emergency meeting of its Supreme Council for National Defense.

incidents.title: US Army LOCUST Directed-Energy Laser Destroys CBP Drone in Friendly-Fire Misidentification, Fort Hancock Texas
incidents.system: AeroVironment LOCUST (Laser Counter Unmanned Aerial System)
incidents.location: Fort Hancock, Texas, USA (US-Mexico border, ~50 miles SE of El Paso)
incidents.description: On February 26, 2026, a US Army counter-drone unit operating an AeroVironment LOCUST directed-energy laser weapon near Fort Hancock, Texas, identified and engaged what appeared to be an unauthorized unmanned aerial system within military-designated airspace along the US-Mexico border. The drone was destroyed. The engaged aircraft subsequently proved to belong to US Customs and Border Protection, which had launched it into military airspace without notifying the military task force — a coordination failure between co-deployed federal agencies. The incident is the first confirmed use of a directed-energy laser weapon to destroy an aircraft in continental US operations, and the first confirmed friendly-fire incident by a US military laser counter-UAS system in domestic airspace. Approximately two weeks prior, CBP personnel had used the same LOCUST system to engage what they believed was a cartel surveillance drone; the target proved to be a Mylar balloon, marking the first continental US laser weapon engagement. Congressional representatives characterized the paired incidents as demonstrating 'policy challenges and impediments the U.S. still faces in defending against drone incursions over the homeland.' The DoD and FAA signed a counter-drone laser safety agreement on April 13, 2026.

incidents.title: Shield AI V-BAT Drone Propeller Severs Romanian Navy Official's Fingers During Training Exercise; Reuters Investigation Documents 50+ Crash Pattern
incidents.location: Off the Texas coast, USA (training exercise aboard a boat)
incidents.description: During a Shield AI training exercise for Romanian Navy personnel aboard a boat off the Texas coast on May 12, 2026, a Romanian Navy official's hand became entangled in the propeller of a V-BAT unmanned aircraft, severing two fingers and fracturing a third. The official underwent emergency surgery on May 12 and a second procedure on May 16 at the University Medical Center in New Orleans; her condition subsequently deteriorated and she was transferred to Walter Reed National Military Medical Center in Maryland, where she remained as of May 25. Shield AI attributed the incident to a violation of established safety procedures rather than a product defect. Romania's Ministry of National Defence confirmed it was investigating. A Reuters investigation published June 5, 2026 reported a broader pattern: the V-BAT has crashed more than 50 times over the prior 18 months among approximately 200 units in Shield AI's internal fleet, a rate exceeding 25%. Named incidents include a February 2026 crash in Texas that ignited a grass fire burning over 40 acres, and a July 2025 detect-and-avoid test in which the V-BAT failed to detect a Cessna aircraft deliberately flown near the drone, forcing the Cessna crew to take evasive action. A prior propeller injury to a US Navy official (date undisclosed) had previously prompted Shield AI to add new landing gear and warning stickers. At least three employees who raised safety concerns were dismissed or departed, and a whistleblower complaint alleging that Shield AI concealed technical flaws to facilitate military sales was filed with the US Department of Labor's Office of Administrative Law Judges in May 2026. Romania maintained its approximately $30 million contract with Shield AI.

incidents.title: Da Vinci X/Xi/5 USM Software Recall: Diagnostic Bypass Allows Defective Arm Assemblies in Clinical Use
incidents.system: Da Vinci X/Xi Surgical System, Da Vinci 5 Surgical System (Universal Surgical Manipulator, part 380647-xx)
incidents.location: United States (31 states) and 16 countries internationally
incidents.description: An FDA Class II recall (Z-1232-2026) was issued on February 2, 2026 covering 219 Universal Surgical Manipulator (USM) components (part 380647-xx) used in da Vinci X, Xi, and da Vinci 5 Surgical Systems. A software implementation error prevented the da Vinci control system from correctly flagging robotic arm assemblies that had failed an internal diagnostic test designed to detect bent and misaligned insertion-axis ball screws — a mechanical condition recognised as a precursor to ball screw fatigue failure and fracture during surgery. As a result, arm assemblies with this condition were permitted to remain in clinical use. The 219 recalled units were distributed across 31 U.S. states and 16 countries.

incidents.title: Foundation Future Industries Phantom MK-1 Humanoid Robots Deployed to Ukraine Combat Theater: Documented Falls During Testing and Lethal-Autonomy Trajectory Raise Deployment-Mismatch Concerns
incidents.location: Ukraine (active conflict zone; specific location undisclosed for operational security)
incidents.description: In February 2026, Foundation Future Industries deployed two Phantom MK-1 humanoid robots to Ukraine's active conflict zone for field testing, marking the first known deployment of humanoid ground robots in an active war theater. The robots were assigned logistics and reconnaissance roles in hazardous areas rather than direct combat. During testing demonstrations, at least one Phantom MK-1 repeatedly fell and struck the ground with a loud crash on multiple occasions, exhibiting locomotion instability in field conditions. The robots also exhibited significant operational limitations: insufficient battery life for sustained deployment, no waterproofing, approximately 20 kg payload capacity, and approximately 20 motors per unit creating multiple mechanical failure points. The company CEO acknowledged that AI hallucination risk in lethal systems is unacceptable while simultaneously stating the robots will need to make fully autonomous decisions in time-critical scenarios — establishing a trajectory toward lethal autonomy without a defined safety architecture for this transition. Foundation secured approximately $24 million in US Army, Navy, and Air Force SBIR research contracts for breaching-operations testing, with the company's LLM-driven autonomy stack designed to reduce teleoperation needs over time. Pentagon Directive 3000.09 compliance is stated, requiring human-on-loop for lethal decisions, but no independent safety assessment of the field deployment has been published.

incidents.title: Waymo Robotaxi With Passenger Drives Into Active Police Crime Scene on Cheshire Bridge Road, Atlanta
incidents.location: Cheshire Bridge Road, Morningside neighborhood, Atlanta, Georgia, USA
incidents.description: An occupied Waymo robotaxi drove past multiple Atlanta Police Department squad cars and uniformed officers to stop in the middle of an active police crime scene on Cheshire Bridge Road, Atlanta. At the time, officers were responding to reports of shots fired at a nearby apartment complex in the Morningside neighborhood; a man had barricaded himself inside after shooting at officers, injuring two (one grazed by gunfire, one with lacerations; both treated and released at Grady Hospital). The Waymo vehicle, carrying a passenger, bypassed visible police vehicles and personnel before stopping autonomously in the restricted area. Waymo stated the vehicle entered an unsecured, untaped lane before stopping. No passenger injuries were reported. The incident prompted Atlanta PD to publish a six-page standard operating procedure for handling Waymo vehicles, which explicitly warns that Waymo systems may not recognize crime scene tape and instructs officers managing extended closures to request a geofence or park a patrol vehicle to block access.

incidents.title: Unitree G1 RL Fall-Recovery Policy Causes Uncontrolled Limb Thrashing, Kicks Operator in Nose
incidents.location: China (specific city unknown; outdoor public performance)
incidents.description: On approximately February 18, 2026, a Unitree G1 humanoid robot lost balance during a public performance in China and fell. Upon falling, the robot's reinforcement learning fall-recovery policy triggered automatically, causing it to thrash its limbs in uncontrolled directions as it attempted to regain its footing. An operator standing nearby tried to catch the robot to prevent it from tipping over; during the RL recovery sequence the robot kicked the operator in the nose, causing heavy bleeding and a possible fracture. Eren Chen, who identified himself as an employee of Booster Robotics, shared the footage on X (formerly Twitter) on February 18, 2026, characterizing the incident as a high-priority safety issue for Unitree to address. Chen noted that similar uncontrolled limb-thrashing behavior during RL fall-recovery appears in other Unitree G1 videos, suggesting the hazard is systematic rather than isolated.

incidents.title: Unitree G1 Robot Strikes Child in Face During Choreographed Dance Performance, Shaanxi Province
incidents.description: On approximately March 21, 2026, a Unitree G1 humanoid robot (approximately 77 lbs, ~35 kg) struck a child in the face during a choreographed dance performance in Shaanxi Province, China. The robot was spinning with arms outstretched as part of its programmed routine when it swung toward the edge of the performance area and made forceful contact with a nearby child's face. Handlers rushed in almost immediately and attempted to restrain the robot, but the robot continued executing its choreographed sequence even as staff intervened. Video of the incident circulated widely on TikTok, YouTube, and X, reigniting discussion about deployment of powerful humanoid robots in public settings without adequate crowd barriers. The child appeared to walk away without serious injury; the extent of injuries was not specified in published reports.

incidents.title: 14-Year-Old Passenger's Foot Trapped Under Waymo Robotaxi for Eight Minutes After Door Opens at Speed, Scottsdale
incidents.location: 92nd Street & Cochise Drive, Scottsdale, Arizona, USA
incidents.description: At approximately midnight on November 19, 2025, a 14-year-old passenger opened the door of a Waymo robotaxi while the vehicle was traveling at approximately 35 mph in Scottsdale, Arizona, and attempted to exit. According to Waymo's incident report, the ADS detected the door opening and executed emergency braking, but the vehicle still ran over the teenager's right foot at 4 mph as it decelerated. The vehicle came to a full stop with its wheel resting on the foot. Emergency services were summoned; the vehicle remained on the foot for more than eight minutes before responders lifted the right side of the vehicle to free the teenager. The teenager was transported to hospital with moderate foot injuries; the foot was not broken. Scottsdale PD investigated and cited the teenager for a curfew violation. An NHTSA incident report was filed. The Phoenix metro area is the only Waymo market where riders aged 14-17 may use the service, via a parent-linked account. The CNN public records investigation (June 3, 2026) surfaced this incident from government records.

incidents.title: Reportedly Hacked AI-Powered Robot Vacuums Allegedly Used for Surveillance and Harassment

incidents.title: Unitree G1 Robot Startles and Hospitalizes 70-Year-Old Woman at Night in Macau Residential Area
incidents.description: In early March 2026, a Unitree G1 humanoid robot being used for promotional activities by a local education center in Macau's Patane district encountered a 70-year-old woman walking on a residential street at approximately 9 PM. The woman, who was looking at her phone, discovered the robot following beside her. Upon noticing the robot she became frightened, exclaiming 'You're making my heart race!' She was subsequently taken to hospital. Macau police responded, escorted the robot from the scene, and detained the 50-year-old operator. The robot was returned to its owner, who was warned to exercise caution when using it in public. The incident drew international media attention, framed by some outlets around the novelty of a humanoid robot being 'arrested.'

incidents.title: Waymo Robotaxi Inches Into Eight Lanes of Oncoming Traffic During Unprotected Left Turn, Chandler Arizona
incidents.location: South Arizona Avenue, Chandler, Arizona, USA (Phoenix metro)
incidents.description: A Waymo robotaxi carrying two passengers — sisters visiting the Phoenix metro area from Virginia for a music festival — began an unprotected left turn across South Arizona Avenue in Chandler, a multi-lane road with traffic moving at approximately 50 mph, and moved slowly into oncoming traffic across multiple lanes. Passengers filmed the incident and reported panicking as the vehicle edged into live cross-traffic. Oncoming vehicles slowed and stopped to allow the robotaxi to proceed; the vehicle paused in the median, yielded to oncoming traffic from the opposite direction, and completed the turn into the far-left lane when a gap appeared. No collision occurred and no injuries were reported. Waymo acknowledged the incident, refunded the fare, and stated it was investigating. The video circulated widely on social media. The incident was among those cited in CNN's June 2026 investigative report on Waymo public records incidents.

incidents.title: Xpeng IRON Humanoid Robot Falls Face-First During Public Debut at Shenzhen Mall

During a choreographed catwalk-style performance before a public crowd, the robot raised its arm as part of the routine and lost balance, pitching forward onto the floor. Three staff handlers were required to drag the 154-pound, five-foot-eight robot away from the crowd. No bystanders were injured. Video of the fall circulated widely and became a trending topic on Chinese social media. Xpeng CEO He Xiaopeng compared the fall to a toddler learning to walk. Xpeng's vice president noted the fall demonstrated the robot was genuinely robotic and not controlled by a hidden performer.

incidents.description: NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison issues a formal letter to AV developers stating the agency has identified "a clear pattern" of driverless AVs interfering with law enforcement and other first responders — driving directly into active emergency scenes, blocking ambulance/fire-apparatus paths, and failing to recognize flashing lights, flares, smoke, fire, and traffic cones; letter explicitly rejects industry "rare edge case" framing ("Emergency scenes are not rare or extreme 'edge cases'"); developers must present concrete engineering fixes by end of July 2026; letter does not name a specific company but follows a documented pattern spanning AV-006 (Austin mass-shooting response blockage), AV-011/AV-015/AV-016 (flooding/construction-zone recalls), AV-018 (Atlanta active crime scene), AV-024 (Waymo Jul 4 SF Presidio gridlock/firework), and AV-025 (Zoox smoke-scene recall) — first cross-industry regulatory directive specifically targeting AV/first-responder interaction as a systemic pattern rather than a single-incident recall
